messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug report describes an infinite loop occurring in HelpFormatter when trying to wrap text that is too long to fit on a single line given the specified width. The testInfiniteLoop test sets the width to 20 characters and provides an option description ("This is a looooong description") that is too long to fit on a line. The HelpFormatter.printHelp method calls printOptions, which in turn calls renderOptions. The renderOptions method eventually calls renderWrappedText to wrap the option description text appropriately.

Inspecting HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText reveals the root cause of the bug: Inside a while(true) loop, renderWrappedText repeatedly tries to find a wrap position (pos) within the width limit. If pos is -1, it appends the remaining text and returns, which is correct behavior. However, if pos is the same as the last position (lastPos), it throws a RuntimeException to avoid an infinite loop.

This safeguard was added specifically to handle CLI-162 (as indicated by the exception message), but the current testInfiniteLoop test does not expect such an exception and instead the code hangs and eventually causes an OutOfMemoryError due to the infinite loop (likely indicating the exception is either not thrown or caught elsewhere in the older version of code).

Thus, the infinite loop occurs because renderWrappedText is trying to wrap a word that is longer than the entire line width. The method findWrapPos fails to find a wrap position before the line width, returning a position equal to the start position, which causes the infinite loop. The out-of-memory symptom happens before the safeguard exception throwing code was introduced or in an environment where this exception is not handled properly.

This diagnosis is consistent with the current bug report description and failing test. The recent bug reports are unrelated, so no additional evidence is drawn from them.

Summary:
- HelpFormatter.printHelp calls printOptions to render each option’s description.
- renderOptions calls renderWrappedText to wrap text descriptions within given width.
- renderWrappedText loops to find wrap positions and breaks text across lines.
- If a word is longer than the width, findWrapPos returns a position that causes an infinite loop.
- This leads to unbounded memory use and JVM crash.
- The infinite loop and out-of-memory error occur due to missing or ineffective handling of overly long words in text wrapping.

The bug can be fixed by improving renderWrappedText to detect when a single word's length exceeds the wrap width and handle it properly instead of looping infinitely. This likely involves handling the case where no wrap position can be found within the width and the word is too long to split normally.

The best method to fix is HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText, as it is directly responsible for the wrap logic and the infinite loop. It may also be valuable to review the findWrapPos method and the overall flow in renderOptions for more robust text wrapping.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
